Error Prone's compiler-based type resolution for this check is reliable, so such warnings are essentially always structurally correct when they fire. Using the non-canonical (inherited) name can mislead readers about where the type is actually declared, especially if InflaterPool is just one of several subclasses of CompressionPool.
runs.issue_signature: nested type referenced via inherited subclass name instead of declaring class
runs.developer_explanation: The field is declared using InflaterPool.Entry, but Entry is actually a nested type defined in the parent class CompressionPool, not in InflaterPool itself. Referring to it through the subclass name can confuse readers about where the type actually lives; it's clearer to write CompressionPool.Entry directly.
